ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Identify and document all direct and indirect beneficial owners, controllers, directors, authorized signatories, and relevant counterparties; screen against United Nations sanctions, European Union restrictive-measures lists, Spanish national sanctions and terrorism-financing information, and applicable domestic law-enforcement or adverse-media sources. Screen against OFAC lists where there is a United States nexus, U.S. person involvement, U.S.-dollar clearing, or a contractual requirement. Apply enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth verification, and enhanced monitoring for PEPs, family members, and known close associates. Spanish obliged entities must apply a risk-based approach under Law 10/2010 and Royal Decree 304/2014 and retain prescribed AML records.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) online name-certification service: https://www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be sufficiently distinctive, must include the legal-form designation or its accepted abbreviation, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. Names are generally filed using the Latin alphabet and may contain Spanish orthographic marks. A local-script version is not generally mandatory. Foreign words and transliterations are permitted subject to distinctiveness, public-order, and non-confusion requirements. The name certificate is issued by the Registro Mercantil Central, while incorporation is completed before a Spanish notary and registration with the competent provincial Commercial Registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any term implying a regulated financial, insurance, governmental, public-interest, or official status without the required authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File a name certificate application with the Registro Mercantil Central, normally proposing up to five names in priority order. If rejected, review the stated identity, similarity, prohibited-term, or formal defect. Submit a corrected application with alternative names and supporting evidence of distinctiveness. A challenge to an RMC refusal may be pursued through the applicable administrative and registry-review mechanisms, including a request for reconsideration or appeal before the competent registry authority and, where legally appropriate, judicial review under the Spanish administrative jurisdiction rules. The incorporation deadline must be monitored because the certificate has a limited validity period; a new certificate should be obtained if the period expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must maintain a registered office in Spain under the Spanish Companies Act, Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable as the registered office if the provider lawfully permits registration, receives official notices, and the company can demonstrate genuine management, records, and operational arrangements. A virtual office is higher risk for a smart-watch and fitness-wearable business involving inventory, product compliance, customer returns, warehousing, imports, employees, or fulfillment. It does not replace premises required for logistics, employment, consumer-protection, product-safety, or tax-substance purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official national percentage is published. For a newly incorporated, non-resident-owned SL using a virtual office and conducting cross-border electronics trading or manufacturing coordination, an internal risk estimate is approximately 10% to 20% for an unannounced or verification-driven physical-address check during the first two years, increasing materially if tax-registration inconsistencies, VAT-risk indicators, customs activity, payroll, product-safety issues, or failed official communications arise. This is a planning estimate, not a statutory probability.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); official e-portal: Sede Electrónica at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; customs and indirect-tax clearance through the AEAT Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Notarize the SL incorporation deed and register it with the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil). 2) Obtain the provisional corporate NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) from the registration process. 3) File Form 036 (Censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) with the local AEAT office to formalize the definitive corporate NIF and IVA (VAT) identity. 4) Apply for a digital certificate (certificado digital) issued by the FNMT to access AEAT e-services. 5) Register in the intra-Community operators census (VIES) via Form 036 when performing EU B2B supplies or acquisitions. 6) Non-resident shareholders receiving taxable payments must obtain their own NIF-N and may need a fiscal representative in Spain.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists; a Spanish SL is per se a Spanish resident corporation under Corporate Income Tax (Law 27/2014). Available statutory elections: (i) 15% reduced corporate rate for newly created entities carrying qualifying economic activity (Art. 29 LIS); (ii) consolidated tax group election via Form 036, requiring a minimum 3-year permanence (Arts. 58-64 LIS); (iii) OSS/IOSS registrations for non-EU distance sales and low-value imported consignments (≤ EUR 150); (iv) special VAT simplified and agriculture/livestock regimes for small businesses; (v) Spanish patent box election for qualifying IP income (Art. 23 LIS). Hybrid mismatch elections are unavailable and are neutralized by Law 11/2021 transposing ATAD/ATAD II.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), governed by Law 37/1992 (LIVA) and Royal Decree 1624/1992
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0: any legal person carrying an economic activity in Spain, including distance sales of smart wearables, must register for IVA/NIF before commencing activity; no minimum turnover threshold applies to resident SLs. For non-Spanish EU suppliers, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 distance-sales threshold applies; imports of consignments up to EUR 150 in value may elect the IOSS special scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2B e-invoicing under Law 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece) becomes mandatory upon entry into force of the implementing Royal Decree, phased in 1 year after publication for enterprises with turnover ≥ EUR 8 million and 2 years for all others. SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) real-time VAT reporting through AEAT web-service APIs already applies to large enterprises (turnover ≥ EUR 6 million) and VAT groups, with an 8-working-day submission deadline (4 days in July). RD 1007/2023 (Veri*Factu) requires certified billing software with digital stamping and QR codes ensuring tamper-proof invoices directly verifiable by AEAT. Export transactions are cleared electronically through the AES customs environment; the SAD/DUA export declaration with MRN serves as the operative fiscal clearance record.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible smartwatch and fitness-wearable goods to third countries (outside the EU) are VAT-exempt with credit (0%) under Art. 21 LIVA once the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the EU; shipment must occur within the legally required term and actual exit must be evidenced. Intra-EU B2B supplies qualify as zero-rated under Art. 25 LIVA where the customer's VIES VAT identification number is valid. Offshore B2B services supplied to third-country recipients fall outside Spanish VAT scope under Arts. 69-70 LIVA; services directly related to exported goods may be zero-rated under Art. 22 LIVA. The exporter must document Incoterms, transport contracts, customs MRN, and customer tax status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD) lodged electronically through AES, with MRN confirmation of exit
Commercial invoice and packing list itemizing the smartwatch and wearable product lines
Bill of Lading (ocean) / Air Waybill (air) / CMR (road) evidencing physical departure from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT TT / LC payment confirmation evidencing FX repatriation
Proof of non-EU or EU customer tax status (foreign tax identification number / VIES validation)
Transit documents (T1/T2) and certificates of origin where preferential duty treatment is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may re-audit export files within the statutory four-year limitation period for VAT self-assessments. Missing or fraudulent export documentation triggers reassessment at 21% IVA plus late-payment interest (interés de demora) calculated from the original filing date. Administrative sanctions under Arts. 184-192 of Law 58/2003 include fixed penalties up to EUR 3,000 for minor infractions, 50%-100% penalties for serious violations, and 100%-150% penalties for fraudulent concealment. Criminal tax fraud under Art. 305 of the Criminal Code applies where the defrauded tax exceeds EUR 120,000, carrying imprisonment of 1-5 years plus fines and possible corporate and director liability. Repeated false zero-rating may result in suspension of the VAT registration, loss of the export exemption, customs debt collection from guarantees, and inclusion in AEAT fraud-prevention reporting.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem and the Single Supervisory Mechanism, with the European Central Bank for monetary operations; foreign-investment registration is administered by the Secretariat of State for Economy and Enterprise Support (Secretaría de Estado de Economía y Apoyo a la Empresa) through the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (Register of Foreign Investments) and the Comisión de Inversiones Exteriores for screening; AML/CFT matters are supervised by the Banco de España, the Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias, and the CNMV for listed instruments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Spain applies EU free movement of capital under TFEU Articles 63-66 and has eliminated all exchange controls effective since 1992. No prior exchange authorization is required for capital injections, repatriations, dividends, or trade settlements. Dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted but subject to the Non-Resident Income Tax Act (Royal Legislative Decree 5/2004), generally a 19% domestic withholding reduced or exempted under applicable tax treaties. Foreign direct investment (FDI) into Spain must be reported to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores for statistical purposes where the investment exceeds €3,000,000, or loans with maturity below one year, via the notary or the relevant bank; no prior approval is required for the smartwatch and fitness-wearable OEM business, which is outside the sectors reserved under Royal Decree-Law 8/2020 (defense, dual-use goods, critical infrastructure, media, or regulated activities). The capital account is thus fully liberalized and profit remittance barriers are limited to standard tax compliance and AML/CDD documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Spain imposes no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio on export proceeds. Exporters may retain EUR or any freely convertible foreign currency in resident or non-resident accounts indefinitely. The receiving bank aggregates all cross-border transactions for the Banco de España balance-of-payments statistical return (Circular 4/2012), including the classification of export receipts under 'Goods' (partida 3100 series). Proceeds may be used directly to settle imports or hedged without conversion to EUR, provided the underlying commercial documentation is available for inspection on request.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury, Medium for ancillary low-value payables. EU-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) passporting into Spain under PSD2 — e.g., Revolut, N26, Qonto, or Spanish-licensed EMIs on the Banco de España register — can provide euro IBANs, SEPA credit transfers, and basic FX conversion. They cannot issue, advise, confirm, or negotiate documentary letters of credit, nor act as the primary counterparty for cross-currency hedging under a CMOF/ISDA master. Non-EU offshore EMIs (UK, Singapore, UAE, Hong Kong) hold no passporting right into Spain and cannot open payment accounts for an SL without a separate Spanish or EU authorization; using them as a clearing rail creates elevated correspondent-bank AML risk, delayed MT103 routing, and subordinated creditor position. Recommended usage: parallel account for small operational expenses and employee reimbursements only; all trade settlements, capital injections, and LC disbursements must be executed through an SSM-supervised credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No mandatory physical attendance at a branch by directors is imposed by Spanish law. Remote onboarding is permitted under Act 10/2010 AML/CFT rules and the Banco de España's interpretation, applying risk-based CDD. For resident directors, a digital certificate (DNIe/electronic ID) or video-identification via the bank's verified channel suffices. For non-resident directors, the standard documentation package consists of: (1) an apostilled notarized power of attorney granted to a local attorney-in-fact or director; (2) a certified copy of the Escritura de Constitución (deed of incorporation) and the certificate of registration from the Registro Mercantil (certificación literal); (3) NIE (foreigner identification number) or passport copies of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners; (4) a sworn-translator (traductor jurado) translation into Spanish where the source documents are in a non-Spanish language; and (5) a notarized UBO declaration (Declaración de Titularidad Real). Banks routinely require one recorded video call with each signatory and, for non-resident shareholders, an original bank reference letter. Physical presence remains a practical accelerator for first AML review but is not a legal threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wholly non-resident beneficial owners with a newly incorporated SL capitalized at the statutory minimum (€3,000) and no established credit history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified registration certificate from the Registro Mercantil; Escritura de Constitución with up-to-date Capital Escrow confirmation; NIE and passport copies of all UBOs/directors; notarized UBO declaration; negative PEP/sanctions screening report; bank reference letter from the shareholder's home institution; 24-month business plan and projected cash flow statements; evidence of Spanish substance such as lease agreement, local warehouse/supplier contracts, or commercial customer orders for smartwatch products.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound shareholder capital injection or intercompany loan exceeding €3,000,000 without prior foreign-investment statistical registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed of capital increase (or loan agreement) filed with the Registro Mercantil; certificate of capital deposit issued by the bank; Form DP-2/DP-3 foreign-investment declaration submitted to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores; SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank; source-of-wealth statement with 12 months of bank statements of the investing entity; consolidated ownership chart evidencing the FDI chain; and the escrow release instruction, if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring cross-border disbursements to high-risk OEM component suppliers (e.g., electronics manufacturers in mainland China) with invoice amounts varying per shipment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed OEM supply agreements with Incoterms 2020 clauses; per-shipment commercial invoices and packing lists; bills of lading or air waybills with the Spanish customs declaration (DUA); supplier corporate registry extract or credit report; quality inspection certificates; payment-schedule reconciliation demonstrating that each MT103 matches a verified invoice; declaration of absence of dual-use or export-controlled components in the smartwatch and fitness-wearable inventory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name-match or near-match alerts against EU, UN, OFAC, or national sanctions lists for UBOs or Chinese supplier legal names.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full sanctions and PEP screening reports generated by a licensed compliance provider; passport and proof of residence for each identified individual; written explanation and organizational chart confirming no beneficial connection to a blocked party; negative-news search results; commodity and end-user attestation for the imported electronic components; and confirmation that the transaction flow does not touch any sanctioned jurisdiction or vessel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency pass-through turnover with same-day onward transfers suggesting treasury-centralization or hidden third-party lending rather than genuine trade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group treasury policy document describing collection and disbursement cycles; underlying sales contracts and EC-sales registers; warehouse logistics evidence (inventory tickets, logistics provider statements in Spain); sworn statement by the statutory auditor confirming the operational nature of the SL; bank transcripts reconciling inflows to purchase orders; and a written undertaking to use no cash-splitting techniques or peer-to-peer settlement layers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity and shareholder loans must be wired by SWIFT MT103 in EUR from the shareholder's own bank account to the SL's operational account, with the bank notified in advance to apply the correct Banco de España balance-of-payments purpose code. For equity capital, the transaction is classified as 'Direct investment in Spain — share capital' (ajuste estatístico de inversión directa), supported by the notarial deed of incorporation or capital increase and the Registro Mercantil certificate; the bank credits the capital escalation only upon receipt of the notary's certificate of deposit. For shareholder loans, the transaction is classified as 'Other investment — loans between affiliated enterprises'; a signed shareholder loan agreement with commercial terms and maturity is required. Any single investment exceeding €3,000,000, or a loan with maturity of less than one year, must be reported by the SL (or its notary) to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores within one month of the transaction. Standard SDD checks apply: source-of-funds documentation for the remitting entity, proof of corporate authority, and sanctions screening. Banco de España receives the bank's aggregated BOP return within the first 15 days of the following month; no pre-wired approval from the central bank is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for the OEM manufacturer: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for all EU supplier and operational invoices (EUR IBAN to IBAN, immediate or same-day); (2) SWIFT MT103 for non-EU suppliers, particularly China-based component vendors, with the full beneficiary bank details and an ISO 20022 remittance identifier; (3) Irrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit governed by UCP 600 for larger OEM procurement contracts, issued by the Spanish bank in favor of the supplier, preferably confirmed by the supplier's local bank (e.g., Bank of China, ICBC, or a Singapore confirming bank) to eliminate country and issuing-bank risk; (4) Documentary Collections (DP/DA) for repeat mid-value shipments where the bank's trade desk mediates document exchange; (5) EUR-denominated disbursements from the SL's operational account using payment-authentication mandates set at onboarding. No prior Banco de España authorization applies to outgoing operational payments, but each MT103 must carry the SL's CIF, the transaction purpose code (e.g., 'Import of goods'), and the underlying invoice reference, and the bank will perform supplementary sanctions and beneficiary-name screening. The SL may also hold a multi-currency position to receive and pay USD/CNH directly, reducing conversion friction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forwards (outrights) under the ISDA 2002 Master or the Spanish Contrato Marco de Operaciones Financieras (CMOF) with the account-holding bank, limited to firm underlying trade exposure.
EUR/CNH deliverable forwards, and EUR/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the PBOC onshore fixing, for hedging mainland-China OEM procurement costs where CNH liquidity is constrained.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNH) to convert long-term shareholder loans or LC-denominated payables into the SL's functional currency.

FX options, zero-cost collars, and participating forwards for asymmetric protection of the EUR revenue base against USD and CNY volatility, executed only with the bank's derivative desk under a signed ISDA/CMOF and collateral agreement.
Short-term FX swaps for liquidity management between the SL's euro and foreign-currency accounts, subject to the bank's credit-limit framework and market-risk haircuts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved within six months after the financial year-end and filed within one month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, the ordinary filing deadline is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine generally EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, subject to statutory calculation rules; repeated non-filing may cause closure of the company registration sheet after one year and restrict subsequent registry filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return, Form 200
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 calendar days of the six-month period following the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, normally 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharges generally range from 1% to 15%, with a 20% surcharge after twelve months plus interest; additional penalties may apply for failure to file or inaccurate filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership declaration included with the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the annual accounts and updated whenever beneficial ownership or control information changes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or inaccurate beneficial ownership information may result in registry objections, filing rejection, administrative sanctions, and restrictions on the validity of registry filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Related-party transactions information return, Form 232, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period; for a 31 December year-end, normally 1 to 30 November. Filing is required only when statutory related-party thresholds or specified transactions apply.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Tax penalties may apply for non-filing, late filing, or inaccurate information; the amount depends on the nature and materiality of the omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Maintenance and annual review of corporate books and registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Relevant Registro Mercantil for mandatory electronic legalization
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Corporate books must be kept current and generally legalized electronically within four months after the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or legalize books may impair evidentiary value, trigger registry objections, and increase exposure to tax, accounting, director-liability, and administrative sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets above EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover above EUR 5.7 million, or average workforce above 50 employees. Mandatory audit also applies to specified regulated, listed, public-interest, subsidized, or other legally designated entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish commercial accounting legislation. IFRS is mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups and may apply in other legally permitted circumstances.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no separate general annual UBO return for every Sociedad Limitada. Beneficial ownership information must be reviewed continuously, updated upon any change in ownership or control, and declared with the annual accounts filing through the Registro Mercantil. Share transfers must be documented, recorded in the Register of Members, and reflected in the beneficial ownership information where applicable.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of beneficial ownership information where required by applicable Spanish registry rules

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 300-1,200 per year, depending on address, mail handling, representation, and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,500-8,000 for a small non-complex Sociedad Limitada; higher fees apply for groups, regulated activities, inventory-intensive operations, or complex related-party transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced CIT for newly incorporated SLs during the first two fiscal years on the first EUR 300,000 of positive taxable base; 23% reduced CIT for enterprises with annual net turnover up to EUR 1 million; R&D and technological innovation tax credits up to 25% of qualifying expenditure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 – Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the AEAT (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) system at www.agenciatributaria.gob.es
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the end of the sixth month after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, generally 1–25 July of the following fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer NIF, corporate name, fiscal year covered, tax regime declarations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Spanish NIF of the corporate taxpayer; non-resident SLs filing through a tax representative must include the representative’s NIF and identification details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Importe neto de la cifra de negocios of the fiscal year, including all sales of smart watches, wearable devices and ancillary services re-invoiced to the Spanish entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents without a Spanish PE, this line is not used for inbound passive income; such income is reported on Form 210 instead. If a PE exists, report the PE’s declared Spanish-sourced revenues.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pérdidas y ganancias before corporate income tax adjustment according to Spanish GAAP and IFRS-accepted measures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers with PE must include PE-attributable income only; overseas head-office adjustments must be eliminated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary adjustments, transfer pricing corrections, depreciation recalculations, and amortisation reversals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the entity is resident, adjustments are compulsory for transactions with related parties. Non-resident PE must include Spanish branch-related transfer pricing adjustments under Article 16 of the CIT Law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 005 – Taxable base and loss offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting taxable base after application of prior years’ negative taxable bases (NOL carryforwards).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities with a Spanish PE may only apply NOLs incurred by that PE in prior years. A non-resident without a PE cannot offset because no Modelo 200 filing arises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cumulative gross CIT after tax credits, withholding, and advance instalments; declaration of credits to be refunded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE, if applicable, must claim any DTA relief under the Spain-treaty and credits already settled on behalf of the branch. If final amount is nil, state zero.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing under Art. 27 LGT: 5% surcharge if filed within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, 20% later plus late-payment interest. If the tax return is not filed: base penalty of 50% of the tax amount with a minimum of EUR 200, plus administrative fines up to EUR 20,000 for missing records, and criminal referral when the evaded amount exceeds EUR 120,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 – Fractional payment of Corporate Income Tax / advanced quarterly payment, filed via AEAT electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within the first 20 days of April, October and December for instalment periods; i.e., for the first 3, 9 and 11 months of the fiscal year. Large taxpayers (net turnover > EUR 10 million) pay an advance of 20% of the taxable base at the statutory rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base from the prior-year tax return (or actual income in certain cases), adjusted for losses and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers with a Spanish PE must file if the PE’s net turnover exceeds EUR 10 million; otherwise the filing may be omitted. No non-resident filing without PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory fractional payment rate, being 23% or 20% depending on turnover, reduced by the capitalisation reserve where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident PE, apply the same scale based on the PE’s turnover and tax base, including permanent establishment remuneration rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting advance payment, after crediting withholding and previous instalments; must be entered even if negative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with a Spanish PE set off taxes already withheld on PE income. If the amount is negative, the filing is still made without payment; refunds are processed in Modelo 200.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to present Modelo 202 or underpaying an instalment triggers late-payment surcharges under Art. 27 LGT (5%–20%) plus interest, and a fixed penalty of EUR 200 per form or EUR 20 per box under Art. 198. Recurrent non-filing may lead to criminal liability when the unpaid balance exceeds EUR 120,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% for residents of an EU/EEA Member State with an effective exchange-of-information agreement and 24% for other non-residents under Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR). Domestic dividend payments to a Spanish corporate shareholder are generally not subject to withholding, but a 19% WHT applies where the recipient is a non-resident individual or company.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief on dividends, the foreign shareholder must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its home tax administration and submit a Form 210 or, where advance relief is sought, deliver the TRC and a dividend ownership declaration to the Spanish paying entity before payment. Relief at source under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive can also be claimed by submitting the standard self-declaration and supporting shareholding and holding-period evidence. Refund claims for excess WHT must be made within the four-year statute of limitation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory IRNR rates: 24% for royalties and interest generally, reduced to 19% for EU/EEA residents with an effective exchange-of-information agreement. The EU Interest & Royalties Directive exemption (0%) applies to royalty and interest payments between qualifying related Spanish and EU companies meeting at least a 10% direct ownership threshold, or the lower 5% threshold available under certain domestic-law provisions. Treaty rates commonly reduce interest WHT to 0–10% and royalties to 5–10% depending on the applicable bilateral treaty and on the existence of a Spanish permanent establishment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 (local currency) per related-party transaction type and related person triggers mandatory Local File documentation; a Master File is mandatory when the worldwide group’s consolidated turnover equals or exceeds EUR 45 million. The annual transfer-pricing information statement (Modelo 232) is mandatory when the total related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a specific Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) equivalent to the UAE, but substantive economic-activity requirements are embedded in the General Anti-Abuse Rule, controlled-foreign-company rules, permanent establishment attribution principles, and anti-treaty-shopping provisions. The wearable-manufacturing SL must justify local employees, operational premises, business decisions, and risk control in Spain to secure treaty benefits and avoid reclassification as a shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-declaring taxable income, overstating deductible expenses, making false statements in Modelo 200, or failing to file the return after exceeding the evaded-amount threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax offence under Art. 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000: imprisonment from 2 to 6 years and a fine of up to 6 times the defrauded amount, plus loss of subsidies and disqualification. Administrative penalty: 50%–150% of the tax adjustment under Art. 191 LGT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors and persons effectively controlling the SL are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt and surcharges under Art. 42 LGT where they caused or permitted the non-compliance. Criminal imprisonment and travel bans (passport surrender) apply to the responsible directors, and the corporate veil is pierced for the enforcement of the economic crime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement Lacking Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Spanish-resident SL as a letterbox to invoice services or hold ownership of IP without real employees, premises, or business decision-making, while claiming tax treaty benefits or intra-group deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The General Anti-Abuse Rule (Art. 15 LGT) permits the tax authority to disregard the arrangement and impose the tax that would have applied without it, including a 50% penalty on the underpaid tax. The anti-abuse provision under Art. 13.1.h of the Spanish CIT Law denies treaty or Directive benefits for artificial arrangements lacking valid economic reasons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participated in creating or maintaining a shell may be joint and severally liable under Art. 42.1.c LGT; in criminal prosecutions for fraudulent insolvency or tax evasion, the director may face disqualification, travel bans, and imprisonment for up to 6 years; the corporate entity’s statute does not shield intentional individuals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register beneficial owners in the corresponding national register, using the Spanish SL to move proceeds without banking controls, or making unexplained cash transactions above statutory thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of Spain’s AML Law 10/2010: administrative fines from EUR 60,001 to EUR 5,000,000 for serious infringements; failure to file annual beneficial-ownership reporting can attract EUR 500–10,000 penalties; criminal money laundering under Art. 301 of the Criminal Code carries 6 months to 6 years of imprisonment and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly use the SL for laundering or concealment of assets face criminal imprisonment and the public prosecutor may obtain provisional seizure of passports or travel bans. The court may order dissolution and liquidation of the company; personal financial liability extends to the full laundered amount when directors acted in concert.
